title: Sleep as going home
hook: a bird tied to a peg flies every direction, then lands where it's tied
carry: in sleep, the self goes home to being

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kumbhakarna slept his strength away, and Krishna asked for yoga is for the one who sleeps in measure in measure.
screen: `YOGA IS FOR THE ONE WHO SLEEPS IN MEASURE IN MEASURE.`

segments.voice: A bird is tied to a peg by a long string. It takes off toward the trees, and the string pulls it up short. It tries the other way, toward the roof. Short again. It tries every direction there is. Finally, worn out, it comes down and settles right at the peg, the one place it was tied all along. That picture comes from Uddalaka, the father who taught his son with an ember. In the very next part of the Chandogya Upanishad, he turns to his son and says: learn from me about sleep.
screen: `A BIRD ON A STRING.` → `EVERY DIRECTION, PULLED SHORT.` → `IT SETTLES AT THE PEG.`

segments.voice: Uddalaka starts with a word. The Sanskrit for he sleeps is svapiti, and the text plays on it: svam apita, gone to his own. When a person sleeps, he says, paraphrased, he has gone home, united with sat, the Existent, being itself. That's why people say he sleeps: he has gone to his own. It's the Upanishad's own wordplay, a teacher's hook, not a dictionary entry. But look at what it does to the night. Sleep stops being a switch-off and becomes a homecoming. Then the bird. Tied to a peg, it flies in every direction, finds no resting place anywhere else, and settles where it's tied. In the same way, Uddalaka says, the mind flies in every direction, finds no resting place elsewhere, and settles down in the breath. For the mind, my dear, is tied to the breath. Three things in the picture. First, the day as flight. Messages, errands, worries, plans: the mind goes out and out, and it's meant to. The bird isn't scolded for flying. Second, the tether isn't a cage. It's what makes landing possible; without the peg, there'd be nowhere to come down. Third, the tether is close. Not a mountain, not a far temple. The breath, going the whole time under all the flying. This is the Upanishads' great teaching in small: your deepest self, atman, is one with sat, being itself, what other Upanishads call Brahman. A few lines on, Uddalaka sums it up for his son: tat tvam asi, you are that. Every night, in his teaching, everyone takes the trip home, whether they notice or not.
screen: `SVAPITI: GONE TO HIS OWN` · `SLEEP AS A HOMECOMING` · `THE BIRD SETTLES AT ITS TETHER` · `THE MIND IS TIED TO THE BREATH`

segments.voice: Let the mind go wherever it likes for a while, tomorrow, yesterday, a conversation, a list, without chasing it back. Each time it tires of a thought, let it come down on one breath, the way the bird comes down at the peg, and then let it fly again if it wants. If you pray, rest in prayer at the landing.
Sleep. In the Chandogya, svapiti, played on as gone to his own: a nightly homecoming, with the mind settling in the breath like a tethered bird. Today's word.
Your line: in sleep, the self goes home to being. The bird flies all day, and lands where it's tied. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Vedanta teachers read Uddalaka's lesson on sleep as a hint about the self, and the tethered bird is used in teaching to show the mind coming to rest in the breath.
